rows.chinese: 莫卧儿的旧帝国曾靠君主的声望维系各省，如今的统治者却必须面对新的问题。法国商人与教官带来了财富和新式兵器，也带来了新的债主。国家需要自己的学校和工场，让地方的赋税变成能够保卫它的力量。
rows.english: The old Mughal empire relied on the prestige of its sovereigns to bind the provinces together. Its rulers now face different demands. French merchants and officers have brought wealth and new weapons, along with new creditors. The state needs schools and workshops of its own to turn provincial revenues into the means to defend it.

rows.english: The empire needs officials who can read its accounts and teachers who can educate the next generation. One college in Delhi cannot serve every province. Paper, teachers and regular funding must reach the districts together.

rows.english: Bengali cloth reaches distant markets, yet the imperial army still relies on ageing equipment. Mines, toolworks and railways can bring these scattered resources together. The arsenals need not supply every purchase, but they must produce more than figures in a ledger.

rows.english: Living under one government does not make its subjects a nation. The provinces have their own languages, faiths and princes. rows.english: Delhi, Nanjing and Paris each have terms to offer the Indian princes. Their rulers seek to preserve more than ancestral palaces: land, revenue and the right to decide their own future are at stake. Cooperation may bring assistance without securing independence.
